hosting_model_findings.rationale: No Program.cs/Startup.cs minimal-hosting pattern, no web.config (none exists in the repo at all, so no AspNetCoreModule* check is even possible), no class deriving from ServiceBase, no BackgroundService/IHostedService. The actual hosting model is a locally-launched Windows Forms desktop executable started via the VB 'My.Application' framework bootstrap (StartupObject = My.MyApplication, which in turn loads MainForm=Form1). This is a double-click/Explorer-launched GUI process on the end-user's own Windows machine — the closest value in the given enum, 'console', is also inaccurate because the app has a GUI message loop (Application.Run against a Form), not a console host.

data_access_findings.rationale: Direct System.Data.OleDb usage (OleDbConnection, OleDbCommand, OleDbDataAdapter, OleDbDataReader) against a single shared Module-level connection; no ORM (no EF Core/EF6/EF-classic DbContext or .edmx, no NHibernate .hbm.xml, no Dapper, no .dbml LINQ-to-SQL mapping) found anywhere in the solution.

connection_strings_in_source_code.value_redacted: Provider=Microsoft.ACE.OLEDB.12.0; data source=<REDACTED-ABSOLUTE-PATH>; Persist Security Info=False;
connection_strings_in_source_code.note: No credentials are embedded (Access/Jet file-based auth has none), but the connection string is hardcoded directly in VB source rather than externalized to App.config's <connectionStrings> section, and the data source is an absolute developer-machine path ('D:\PROGRAMING\Visual Basic\Flat Design\Flat Design\Flat Design\studentDB.accdb'). This is a portability/deployment finding, not a credential-leak finding: the app will fail to connect on any machine other than the original author's, including the CI/discovery environment used for this pass.

config_and_secrets_surface.app_config_summary: App.config contains only a <startup><supportedRuntime .../></startup> element pinning the CLR to v4.0/.NET Framework 4.8; it defines no <connectionStrings>, <appSettings>, or <system.webServer> sections. This is expected for a WinForms app with a hardcoded in-code connection string, but it also means the standard 'four places connection strings hide' check (web.config / app.config / appsettings.json / user-secrets) under-reports for this app — the actual connection string is in a fifth, non-standard location (a VB code module), which this pass additionally scanned per the data-access methodology step.

findings.summary: Hosting-model enum (iis-aspnet | iis-aspnet-core-module | kestrel-selfhost | windows-service | worker-service | console) has no value for a locally double-click-launched WinForms GUI process; closest-available value 'console' is misleading because the app runs a GUI message loop.

SQL-injection vector in ViewForm's search feature: LoadSData builds the WHERE clause by direct string concatenation of unsanitized user input (txtSearch.Text) instead of using a parameterized OleDbCommand/OleDbDataAdapter.SelectCommand.Parameters, unlike every other data-access call site in this solution (InsertForm/EditForm/the delete path all use .Parameters.AddWithValue correctly).

Hardcoded absolute developer-machine file path for the Access database connection string, embedded in source rather than externalized to App.config; the app cannot connect on any other machine without a source-code edit and rebuild.

The .vbproj references a ClickOnce signing key file ('Student Management System Siddharth Jain_TemporaryKey.pfx' via ManifestKeyFile, with SignManifests=true and GenerateManifests=true) that does not exist anywhere in the repository tree. A clean checkout cannot reproduce a signed-manifest build without the missing key.
